clue.text: Dull group absolutely determined

parts.note: dull means dead, lifeless or flat
a set is a group of things or people

explanation.surface: A boring band of people who are nonetheless utterly resolute.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dead set on a goal is fixed and resolute about it, an idiom for firm resolve.

clue.text: Fed up with expert's damage

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word Fed is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written
an ace is an expert; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Someone sick of a specialist who vandalises things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' looks like one phrase meaning annoyed, but 'up' is the reversal signal: FED read upwards gives DEF.
explanation.definitionFit: To deface something is to spoil or mar its surface, a synonym for damage as a verb.

clue.text: A quiet look with which medic shows coolness

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
lo is an old word meaning look or behold
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor's calm glance reveals composure.
explanation.definitionFit: Aplomb is self-assurance under pressure, a synonym for composure or coolness.

clue.text: Scenery pal organised according to script

indicators.note: organised means the letters of scenery and pal are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A friend sets up the stage scenery, following the written instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges SCENERY PAL; 'according to' is a link, and the definition is 'script'.
explanation.definitionFit: A screenplay is the written text of a film, so it is a kind of script.

clue.text: Thus Dorothy turns up and fusses

indicators.note: in a down clue, turns up means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: so means thus, in that way
Dot is a short form of the name Dorothy

explanation.surface: A woman called Dorothy arrives and makes a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' sounds like arriving, but it reverses SO + DOT, giving TODOS.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a commotion, so the plural names bouts of bother or fuss.

clue.text: Ice cream put down in Italian house

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed within the other here

parts.note: casa is the Italian word for house
sat is a past tense meaning set or put down, as in sat the baby on the chair

explanation.surface: Someone places an ice cream on the table inside an Italian home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put down' suggests placing or insulting, but here it is simply the past tense sat; the container signal is 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassata is a Neapolitan layered ice cream dessert with candied fruit, an example of the dessert.

clue.text: Restrict prisoner's exercise

parts.note: a con is a convict or prisoner; the 's gives the S
to train is to exercise or work out

explanation.surface: Limits are placed on an inmate's workout.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain is to hold back or limit, a synonym for restrict.

clue.text: Got rid of building in garden?

explanation.surface: A gardener disposed of an outbuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed is to cast off or discard; a shed is also a simple hut for tools at the bottom of a garden.

clue.text: Three a's — medic set out for university life

indicators.note: set out means the letters of these words are laid out in a fresh order

parts.note: three a's gives the letter A three times

explanation.surface: A doctor arranges three grade-A results to win a place at college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' rearranges AAA plus MEDIC; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Academia is the world of scholarship and higher learning, the life led at a university.

explanation.surface: A perfect score, but is everything fine?
explanation.walkthrough: A test marked 10/10 has every answer correct; the phrase is also a casual way of asking whether someone is well.
explanation.definitionFit: Full marks means every answer is correct; the phrase also serves as a synonym for satisfactory or fine.

clue.text: Office worker given five pounds, turning five into fifty

indicators.note: Roman five is V and Roman fifty is L, so the V in the banknote word is swapped for L

parts.note: a fiver is a five-pound note

explanation.surface: A clerk receives a banknote and somehow multiplies its value tenfold.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman numeral V (five) in FIVER becomes L (fifty). A fiver is British slang for a five-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A filer is a clerk who files documents, a kind of office worker.

clue.text: Room in which a twister may operate

definitions.text: Room in which a twister may operate

parts.words: Room in which a twister may operate
parts.note: a twister suggests a tornado or a swindler, but here it is a person twisting to music, and the room is where they would do it

explanation.surface: A space where a tornado or a con artist might be at work.
explanation.walkthrough: The twist was a 1960s dance, so a twister is a dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dance hall is a large public room hired for dancing, where people would do the twist.

clue.text: Repay firm friend — pounds to be received

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: to be received means the friend word takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: a mate is a friend
pens are enclosures or pounds for animals

explanation.surface: Paying back a business partner, with money due to come in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pounds' looks like money, but it means animal enclosures; 'to be received' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To compensate someone is to make amends or reimburse them, a synonym for paying back.

clue.text: Special sort of shop — I was first to go back

indicators.note: to go back means the pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: led means was first, at the front

explanation.surface: A customer boasts of being at the front of the queue as they go back to a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go back' reverses I + LED, giving DELI.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling fine or specialist foods.

clue.text: A duke opposing worker — old and privileged

parts.note: V is short for versus, meaning against or opposing
an ant is the classic crossword worker, from the worker ant
aged means old

explanation.surface: An aristocrat set against an elderly labourer who enjoys favours.
explanation.definitionFit: Advantaged means having a better position or more resources, a synonym for privileged.

clue.text: Food available from Kent town after golf tournament

indicators.note: after means the Kent town comes behind the golf event in the answer

parts.note: the Open is golf's oldest championship
Sandwich is a town in Kent, England

explanation.surface: Snacks sold in a Kent town once a golf championship is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandwich is a town in Kent, the English county, and the Open has been played at nearby Royal St George's.
explanation.definitionFit: An open sandwich is a single slice of bread with toppings, an example of a light meal.

clue.text: The pale colour of a flower

definitions.text: The pale colour of a flower

parts.words: The pale colour of a flower
parts.note: flower is read as something that flows, a river, so the clue asks for a pale shade named after an African river

explanation.surface: A soft hue seen in the petals of a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords a flower is often a river, as it flows.
explanation.definitionFit: Nile green is a pale bluish-green shade, supposedly the tint of that river's water.

clue.text: Tripped over in street, 'umiliated

parts.note: humiliated means humbled; the apostrophe shows the H dropped, as in Cockney speech, giving the word without its H

explanation.surface: Someone falls flat on the pavement and is embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''umiliated' signals a dropped H, so HUMBLED loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To stumble is to trip or lose one's footing, so stumbled matches tripped over.

clue.text: Put in jail with gangster inside

parts.note: to intern is to confine or imprison someone
Al Capone is the archetypal gangster

explanation.surface: A mobster is locked up along with the other inmates.
explanation.definitionFit: Internal means on the inner side, a synonym for inside as an adjective.

clue.text: What could be on the gallant — or on the cowboy

definitions.text: What could be on the gallant — or on the cowboy

indicators.note: could be means the letters of on the gallant might be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A dashing man and a cowboy might both wear the same headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges ON THE GALLANT, and the whole clue describes headwear that might sit on either man.
explanation.definitionFit: A ten-gallon hat is the tall, wide-brimmed headgear typical of a Western rancher.

clue.text: Failing within company

parts.note: in means within
a firm is a company

explanation.surface: A struggling business on its last legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Infirm means weak or frail, especially through age, a synonym for failing as an adjective.

clue.text: All together in France originally

parts.note: the clue describes a phrase meaning all together that was borrowed from French

explanation.surface: Everyone united in France at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'All together'; 'in France originally' tells you the phrase comes from French.
explanation.definitionFit: En bloc is a borrowed French phrase meaning as a whole or all at once.

clue.text: Appropriate food from what is said

indicators.note: from what is said means the word for food is spoken and the answer shares its sound

parts.note: meat is food

explanation.surface: Suitable meals according to rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like a verb (to take) but is an adjective meaning suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Meet is an old adjective meaning fitting or proper, as in meet and right.

clue.text: Substance in body — a s-surfeit gets in repeatedly

parts.note: a glut is a surfeit, and the stammered s-surfeit repeats the first letter of that word

indicators.note: repeatedly means the word in is written twice in a row

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A stammered complaint about too much of something entering a body again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter 's-surfeit' tells you to stutter the synonym too: GLUT becomes G-GLUT.
explanation.definitionFit: An agglutinin is an antibody in the blood that makes cells clump, a substance found in the body.

clue.text: More than a bottle of wine? One's drunk, getting about

definitions.text: More than a bottle of wine?

parts.note: lit is slang for drunk
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone has had over a bottle of wine and is drunk and wandering about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' is a link here (one is drunk). A standard wine bottle holds 75 centilitres, so this measure is slightly more.
explanation.definitionFit: A litre is a metric measure of 100 centilitres, larger than the usual 75cl wine bottle.

clue.text: Way is simple, then hard

parts.note: pat means glib or too simple, as in a pat answer
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A method is easy at first, then difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: A path is a track or route, a synonym for way.

clue.text: Secure a guy, someone to manage the estate

parts.note: to land is to secure or win, as in land a job
gent is short for gentleman, a guy

explanation.surface: Hiring a man to look after a country property.
explanation.definitionFit: A land agent is a steward employed to run a landed property for its owner.

clue.text: What's gross, bad and grating

parts.note: gr is the abbreviation for gross, twelve dozen
ill means bad, as in ill feeling

explanation.surface: Something disgusting, nasty and irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grating' looks like an adjective meaning irritating; it is a noun, a lattice of bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A grill is a framework of metal bars, a synonym for a grating.

clue.text: Supposedly intelligent creature? No DPhil in the making

indicators.note: in the making means the letters of No and DPhil are being formed into something new

explanation.surface: A clever animal that never earned a doctorate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the making' rearranges NO DPHIL. A DPhil is the doctorate at Oxford, a nod to the creature's supposed brains.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolphins are marine mammals widely held to be among the cleverest animals.

clue.text: Men die, roughly 100, as the result of disease

indicators.note: roughly means the letters of men and die are arranged loosely into a new order

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: About a hundred men die from an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' looks like an estimate of the number, but it rearranges MEN DIE. 'as the result of' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, an endemic is an illness constantly present in a given region or population.
